display.purpose: Every name, title and button label, uppercase; sized by the caller (the phone lobby name field shown, shrinking to fit a long name; the lobby ready button is 2.875rem). Display surfaces size it in --cu: countdown 16, game name 15, play title 8, plaque 6.4 (compact 2.6), announcement 5.5, join heading, notice and open-room button 5.4, game plaque 3.4, roster name 3.2 (shrinking to fit its column for a long name), top tag 2.2.

headline.purpose: Outcome band title on the phone.

plaque.purpose: The four-letter room code on the enamel plaque.

title.purpose: Player name beside their top on the phone.

body.purpose: Running text on the legal page.

label.purpose: Cues, statuses, seat states, band detail, the play header subtitle, the roster cue and its ready mark, the back-to-games control, the player count on the game choice and the phone lobby's ready count.

small.purpose: The site footer and notes on the legal page.

shadows.name: screen-shadow-raised
shadows.value: 0 calc(var(--cu) * 0.5) calc(var(--cu) * 1.2) color-mix(in oklab, var(--lacquer-ink) 40%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: QR card, plaques (room code and chosen game), roster and brass button on the display; set by the display.units mixin.

shadows.name: plaque-inlay
shadows.value: inset 0 0 0 4px var(--enamel), inset 0 0 0 7px var(--ivory), 0 4px 10px color-mix(in oklab, var(--lacquer-ink) 40%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Enamel plaque with its ivory inner filet (phone values, the same plaque.enamel mixin at a 7px filet raised by --shadow-phone-raised; the display uses the plaque.enamel mixin: an enamel inset at 56 % of --plaque-filet, then the ivory filet, then the raised shadow).

shadows.name: walnut-frame
shadows.value: inset 0 0 0 calc(var(--cu) * 0.5) var(--walnut), inset 0 0 0 calc(var(--cu) * 0.7) color-mix(in oklab, var(--walnut) 55%, var(--lacquer-ink))

shadows.name: brass-inlay
shadows.value: inset 0 0 0 calc(var(--cu) * 0.4) var(--brass-deep), inset 0 0 0 calc(var(--cu) * 0.7) var(--brass)
shadows.purpose: Inner filet of the brass button on the display (brass-button.brass mixin).

shadows.name: shadow-phone-lobby-top
shadows.purpose: Large spinning top in the phone lobby (filter).

shadows.name: shadow-phone-control
shadows.purpose: Brass retry button and the lobby's ready button (unpressed) on the phone.

shadows.name: countdown-text
shadows.value: 0 calc(var(--cu) * 0.5) calc(var(--cu) * 1.2) color-mix(in oklab, var(--lacquer-ink) 40%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Text shadow under the countdown numerals over the arena (the raised-object values).

shadows.name: scene-shadow-catcher
shadows.value: ShadowMaterial lacquer-ink, opacity 0.38, PCF soft shadow radius 5
shadows.purpose: Shadows the modelled tops cast on the 3D arena plan.

motion.name: transition-fast
motion.purpose: Press scale, hover fill, knob follow, gauge opacity. Value comes from @adrienlcp/styles tokens.defaults.

motion.name: transition-base
motion.purpose: Stick base re-anchoring, pad fade when inert.

motion.name: transition-slow
motion.purpose: Band wipe (clip-path), seat ground change; multiples drive spins (x2 status ring, x6 won top, x15 lobby top).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for wipes and presses.

motion.name: dash-refill
motion.purpose: Cooldown ring refilling from dashoffset 101 to 0.

motion.name: countdown-beat
motion.value: var(--transition-slow) cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), from opacity 0 and scale 1.25
motion.purpose: Each countdown number beating in over the arena.

motion.name: announcement-wipe
motion.value: clip-path var(--transition-slow) var(--ease-out); in from inset(0 100% 0 0), out to inset(0 0 0 100%)
motion.purpose: The display announcement band wiping in from the left and out to the right.

motion.name: top-spin
motion.value: 3 rad/s; lean 0.35 per unit speed up to 0.3 rad; a fall slides to the middle of the ditch, drops to its floor in 0.55 s and lies down along it, its spin dying
motion.purpose: Modelled tops in the 3D arena; reduced motion stops the spin.

motion.name: hold-to-leave
motion.purpose: The brass arc filling the back-to-games ring while held; it empties at once on release.

breakpoints.name: portrait
breakpoints.purpose: The phone pad's portrait sizing and thumb line; the outcome band stacks. Never a prompt to turn.

narrative.overview: A table game on a walnut drum. On the display the arena is a low turned drum standing on the floor of the Looking Glass alcove, seen from the front over a solid lacquer-ink backdrop: a billiard-green felt platform raised inside a ditch, ringed by a walnut lip with a brass filet and a brass band. Every structure on the felt and in the shell (arena rim, ticks, centre ring, rules between zones, tally pips, cooldown gauge) is a brass filet, never a modelled object. The objects that sit on the table are the furniture of a café: lacquered spinning tops in six seat colours, an enamel-blue plaque for the room code, an ivory QR card, a slate scoreboard framed in walnut. The phone is the same table seen through one seat: its whole ground turns that seat's lacquer and carries the player's own top.
keyCharacteristics: A walnut drum standing in the alcove over a solid lacquer-ink backdrop; felt and brass filets for every line and ring, no gradients, no glass.
Six lacquered tops, each with a carved glyph, so seats differ by shape as well as colour; flat SVG on every 2D surface, modelled only inside the 3D arena.
The 3D arena is a walnut drum seen from the front, 20° above level, framed to 90 % of its row and centred in it; every colour it draws comes from the CSS tokens.
Big Shoulders Display Black, uppercase, for everything named; Barlow Semi Condensed for everything read.
Depth from soft ink-tinted shadows and inset double filets, never from blur or glow.
Display sized in `--cu` units inside a 3 % safe area, the game choice included; controller sized in rem and `--pad-unit`.

rules.name: The Filet Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn, not filled: a ring, a rule, a tick or a gauge is a brass stroke on felt or slate, with opacity carrying its rank. No filled shapes stand in for lines.

rules.name: The Lacquer Rule
rules.body: The six seat lacquers are the only saturated colours, and they appear only as a seat: a top, a phone ground, a named seat. A seat colour never decorates anything that is not a player.

rules.name: The Two Marks Rule
rules.body: A seat is always shown by its top (lacquer plus carved glyph) and its name together, never by colour alone. The name is the one the player picked on their phone (12 characters at most), or the seat's colour until they pick one. In the arena, the modelled top carries a name tag hung above it. The game choice's demo tops are nobody's seat, so they go unnamed.

rules.name: The One Source Rule
rules.body: The 3D scene owns no colour. It resolves every token (`--felt`, `--brass`, `--seat`, `--seat-cap`, `--seat-mark`, `--seat-top-ring`, `color-mix` included) through a hidden probe in the page and draws without tone mapping, so the lacquer on the table is the lacquer in the roster.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: The body face ships 500 and 700 only; anything heavier than regular is written 700, and font synthesis is off.

rules.name: The Names Are Capitals Rule
rules.body: What a player must read from across the room (a name, the code, an outcome) is in the display voice; everything else is a label in the body face.

rules.name: The Ink Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is soft, offset downward, and tinted with lacquer ink between 30 and 40 %; the 3D scene's grounded shadows go to 50 %. No hard offsets, no glow, no coloured shadows.

rules.name: The Drum In The Alcove Rule
rules.body: The arena is an object standing on the alcove's floor, seen from the front over a solid, unlit backdrop; the scene never draws the alcove's floor or walls. On the felt, the rim, ticks and centre ring stay unlit filets at their 2D radii and opacities; depth comes from the drum's walnut and brass, the tops, their light and their grounded shadows.

dos: **Do** draw every ring, rule, tick and gauge as a brass filet, ranking them by opacity (100 / 70 / 55 / 40 %).
